Latest code discovered in the WhatsApp TestFlight beta reveals that Meta is exploring an alternative to iCloud backups for iPhone users. Details below.

WhatsApp is developing its own backup service

According to findings by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is developing its own cloud backup service for iPhone users as an alternative to iCloud.

The feature is not yet available to TestFlight beta users, but WABetaInfo has successfully enabled the relevant interface, allowing users to choose between iCloud and WhatsApp's own cloud service as their backup destination. The interface indicates that 2GB of free storage will be provided, and the report also mentions that a paid plan could offer up to 1TB of capacity.

The report also points out that users can currently choose whether their WhatsApp backups on iCloud use end-to-end encryption, while WhatsApp's own backup system will set end-to-end encryption as the default option.

Although no official launch timeline has been announced, the report notes that WhatsApp is also developing an alternative to Google Drive backups for Android users. Given that work on both platforms is underway, the new feature could be officially announced in the near future.
